name: EmbeddingGemma 2
purpose: On-device multimodal embeddings (text, image, video, audio in one 768-d space) for search and RAG on phones and laptops; encoders loadable separately.

license.name: Apache-2.0 (Gemma 4 license page)
license.notes: Card header and card metadata both say Apache 2.0 and link ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license; that page (read through a summarizer after a redirect) is the standard Apache License 2.0 text. The card body additionally says 'Deployments must adhere to the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy': that is a policy reference, not a clause of the Apache text; the inconsistency is on the card itself. HF createdAt 2026-09-14.

architecture.kind: encoder-style transformer, 24 layers, mean pooling, 5:1 local-global attention, 1024 sliding window
architecture.why_this_design: Runs on consumer hardware with low latency; selective encoder loading (text 270M, +image 440M, +audio 570M, full 740M); MRL to 512/256/128; task prefixes steer embeddings.

engine_support.notes: A GGUF exists (ggml-org/embeddinggemma-2-GGUF, Q8_0 text 310 MB plus mmproj 555 MB) but llama.cpp build 9750 failed with "unknown model architecture: 'gemma-embedding2'" on 2026-10-07 (user report); re-check current llama.cpp.

benchmarks.name: Note search, 60 queries over 813 notes: recall@5 (v1 vs v2)
benchmarks.variant: EmbeddingGemma 2 vs 1, Apple M1 Max, float32 MPS; small personal test

benchmarks.name: Code search, 10 questions over 424 files: correct file ranked first

strengths: highest MTEB Code number among small models read (vendor)
weaknesses: trails Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B on multilingual text (61.36 vs 64.33, vendor numbers)
omitting the task prefix lowers quality
soft.maturity: Google; second generation of the line.

user_reports.summary: Retrieval better than v1, but cost higher: indexing 813 notes took 138.8 s vs 81.8 s, peak RSS 2.75 GiB vs 1.03 GiB (float32 on MPS). The author could not switch because llama.cpp could not load the v2 GGUF.

Vendor-run comparison: nearly 3 points behind Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and 9.22 behind the 8B on multilingual text, ahead of 0.6B on MTEB Code (78.68 vs 75.41); 542 MB resident versus 5.8 GB for Qwen3-0.6B under Ollama defaults.

tona_fit.reason: Apache-2.0 (text read), 270M text core plus image/video/audio encoders, MTEB Code 78.68 (vendor) and the smallest memory footprint of the strong embedders; multilingual text trails Qwen3-Embedding. Best where memory is tight or multimodal retrieval is wanted.
